questions.prompt: Why does the big blind defend more hands than the small blind against the same open?

choices.text: The big blind already has 1bb in the pot and closes the action.
The big blind acts first postflop.
The small blind is required to call.
The big blind can only fold or all-in.

questions.explanation: You are getting a discount and no one acts behind you preflop. You still play out of position.

questions.prompt: Small blind versus a button open at 100bb. What is the preferred shape?

choices.text: Call every hand that is not trash, then play out of position.
Prefer 3-bet or fold over a flat.
Complete every hand because you already posted.
Fold AA so you can trap later.

questions.explanation: The small blind is the worst seat. Flatting a wide range out of position is the leak.

questions.prompt: Button opens, you are the big blind with 72o and 100bb. Best action?

choices.text: Call. The big blind defends 100% of hands.

questions.explanation: A discount is not a reason to play the worst hand. 72o still folds to a button open.

questions.prompt: Button opens, you are the big blind with AJo. Folding is…

choices.text: Required, because the big blind must fold offsuit hands.

questions.explanation: AJo is a standard big-blind continue against a steal, unlike against a tight UTG open.
